discovery: Conception and construction of the Large Hadron Collider and its general-purpose detectors ATLAS and CMS, which enabled the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson

nominees.name: Peter Jenni
nominees.affiliation: CERN, Geneva, Switzerland, and Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg, Germany

subfield: Experimental particle physics and accelerator/detector instrumentation
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism. The instruments that turned that prediction into a 2012 discovery have never been recognised. Lyn Evans led the design and construction of the LHC: 1232 superconducting dipoles at 8.3 tesla in a two-in-one design, operating at 1.9 K. It is the most complex scientific instrument ever built. Michel Della Negra and Peter Jenni conceived and founded CMS and ATLAS. These were the first detectors able to separate rare signals from about a billion proton collisions per second, using radiation-hard silicon tracking, high-resolution calorimetry and large muon systems. Their concepts set the standard for experiments since. These instruments found the Higgs boson, measured its couplings and now set the frontier for searches for new physics. This nomination recognises the invention and construction of the tools that let physics see the scalar sector.
